newsitem.title: USA: ARCO, Alaska to seek injunction against Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: ARCO, Alaska to seek injunction against Greenpeace.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co. (ARCO) and the state of Alaska will seek an injunction against environmental group Greenpeace early Friday in federal court, a company spokesman said.

Starting at 9:30 a.m. PDT (1630 GMT), the parties will ask federal judge Russell Holland in Alaska to keep Greenpeace away from a mobile drilling rig, which ARCO intends to begin towing on Friday from the Prudhoe Bay oil fields toward a new offshore site.
ARCO and Alaska sought injunctions separately, but the judge decided to hear their case together.
"We want a permanent injunction to prevent (Greenpeace) from harassment of our vessel," Al Greenstein, an ARCO spokesman said.

The company also wants an 500 meter safety zone, which Greenpeace cannot enter, to apply to both state and federal waters. The rig, moored 75 miles (120 km) west of its destination, is protected by the zone in state waters only.
Greenpeace has stationed a vessel in front of the rig, but is obeying the safety zone, a member said earlier.
The group maintains that moving the rig will disturb marine mammals and threaten a nearby wildlife refuge once it reaches the drill site.
